Second, and this is the one the whole `reference` field exists for: the sim category's own note warns that 'conforming a game for four-to-eight-year-olds to MLB's strikeout rate is the mistake this field exists to prevent'.

measured.over: 878 games / 50,004 plate appearances / 254,128 pitches, 8 seeds x 3 venues, all 30 kids

gameShape.whatIsPLAUSIBLE: Runs per game at 5.34 is a lot of scoring, and for a kids' game that is arguably correct. The batted-ball split (60/15/15/10 ground/line/fly/popup) is ground-heavy in the way a child swinging under a pitch should be, and exit velocity means 50.2mph against sim.batSpeed's band.
gameShape.whatIsNot: BABIP 0.678, against real baseball's ~0.300. PR 9 moved it from .713 WITHOUT TOUCHING THE DEFENCE -- fewer grounders is fewer of the class that goes for hits 81.4% of the time -- and claims no credit for a fix it did not make. The cause is unchanged and measured: grounders are 81.4% hits because an infielder facing the median 51mph grounder covers 6.5ft of an 18ft half-gap, most of that lost to a 0.39s read and a standing-start acceleration ramp. The contributing records are unchanged: the arm band (sim.throwSpeed), the reach (sim.catchRadius, 3ft against v1's 11.36), and the deferral of tag-ups. AND THE SECOND NUMBER: a 42.4% strikeout rate, which sim.retuneTargets now records as LOAD-BEARING -- removing it without fixing the defence takes runs per game from 4.9 to 15.4. PR 10 moves both, together, because the sweep proved they cannot move apart.
gameShape.performanceNote: A game costs ~140ms once the release memo is warm, or 2.25ms per plate appearance -- so PR 8's 50,000 is about 113 seconds. Getting there took two fixes worth naming: the pitcher aims at a SPOT so the release solve is memoisable (13.6ms to a cache hit), and the defence RE-READS the ball without RE-TRACING it (the trajectory does not change between ticks, so re-computing the prediction produced an identical answer for two thousand RK4 steps). Together, 1.7s per game to 0.14s.
gameShape.whatWouldClose: It does not close -- it is a `note`, now carrying the real measurement PR 8 promised. Its job is to hold the numbers BEFORE anyone starts tuning, so PR 9's retune has a before. The instrument that produced them is described in sim.harnessMethod, including what it cannot see.

reading.over: 874 games / 50,045 plate appearances / 256,019 pitches, 8 seeds x 3 venues, roster rotated so all 30 kids bat
20 games, 6 innings, park venue, ROSTER[0..8] vs ROSTER[9..17]

andBefore.why: ★ NOT JUST A BIGGER SAMPLE -- A DIFFERENT SIM. The 1,166-PA reading was taken over a resolveSwing that clamped a missed bat into a graze at exactly 90 degrees (sim.contactGeometry), so its 25.6% strikeout rate and 0.624 BABIP were computed with 30% of fair balls being swings that never touched the ball. Both readings are kept because the old one is what a plausible-looking total looks like when the distribution underneath it is broken, and that is worth more than either number.

supersedes.why: ★ THE SECOND SUPERSESSION, AND THE THREE READINGS TELL A STORY WORTH KEEPING. The 1,166-PA reading (K 25.6, BABIP .624) was taken over a resolveSwing that clamped a missed bat into a graze at 90 degrees. The 50,045-PA reading (K 43.0, BABIP .713) was taken after that fix but before there was a swing plane, so the mean batted ball left at 0 degrees. This one is the first taken over a sim where a bat that misses misses and a swing has a plane. Keeping all three is what makes 'every total stayed plausible' checkable rather than asserted.

lineupArm.what: A lineup planner that knows a shortstop needs an arm.
lineupArm.why: sim.gapBallOutcome.theArmAtShort recorded the finding and deferred the fix: systems/lineup.ts autoAssign scores shortstop on `fielding*2 + speed` and CENTRE FIELD on `fielding + speed*2` -- it puts the best arm on the mound and then never looks at `pitching` again. That was harmless in v1, where every throw was 9.65x runner speed and the catch radius was 11.4ft, so arm strength bound nothing. With real throws it put a 34mph arm (77ft of range) at the position with the longest routine infield throw, and the routine grounder to short became a single.
lineupArm.whyNotTheBestArm: The v2 shortstop reaches 86.6ft, not the roster's best 154 — because the mound takes the best arm and the demand ordering then puts the next three in left, right and behind the plate, all of which throw further than short does. That is the derivation working rather than a compromise: 86.6ft comfortably covers the 68.2ft throw, where v1's 77ft did not once the fielder had moved off his post.
lineupArm.theArmWeightIsDERIVED: ★ NOBODY STATES THAT LEFT FIELD NEEDS AN ARM. Each position's demand is the distance from its post to the bag it actually throws to, read out of FIELD_POSITIONS -- infielders to first, outfielders and the catcher to second. So if the field changes, the lineup follows, and the ordering (LF/RF > C > CF > 3B > SS > 2B) is a consequence of the park rather than a table somebody maintains.
lineupArm.v1IsUNTOUCHED: src/systems/lineup.ts is v1 code on v1's bundle path, and AGENTS.md is explicit that a v2 change altering dist/assets/main-*.js is a bug. planDefence is a new file in src/v2/sim/; autoAssign keeps its own behaviour and its own tests, and a v2 test asserts the two differ in the direction this record claims.

value.weights: arm = throwDemandFt(pos) normalised, x2; plus traffic x fielding and range x speed

lineupArm.whatWouldClose: Nothing here. What it hands forward is whether an arm-aware defence changes BABIP enough to matter, which is PR 8's to answer -- the planner is one of the levers PR 9 has.

contactGeometry.what: That a bat which passes more than (r_ball + r_barrel) from the ball's centre MISSES it, rather than grazing it at the steepest angle two circles can touch at.
contactGeometry.why: ★ THE HARNESS'S FIRST FINDING, AND IT WAS FOUND BY A HISTOGRAM RATHER THAN A TOTAL. resolveSwing turns the undercut into a launch angle through asin(offset / centreSep), and for three PRs it CLAMPED the offset into that separation first. The code comment beside the clamp said 'Beyond that separation the bat misses the ball entirely, which is what the clamp means' -- but a clamp means the opposite of a miss. asin(±1) is exactly ±90 degrees, so every swing that had actually gone by underneath the ball was recorded as a ball hit perfectly straight up or straight down.
contactGeometry.howItHid: Every TOTAL stayed plausible. GameTally counted these as balls in play and was right to; sim.gameShape reported a 25.6% strikeout rate that nobody would question; contact.test.ts asserts Nathan's identity SYMBOLICALLY, which is a claim about exit SPEED and says nothing about where the bat was; and 982 tests passed over it. What it could not survive was a distribution: 22% of fair balls in the single 5-degree bin at the top of the launch-angle scale, and 8% more at the bottom.
contactGeometry.theGeometry: Two circles intersect when the distance between their centres is at most the sum of their radii. centreSep = BALL_RADIUS_FT (0.1207) + BAT.BARREL_RADIUS_FT (0.104) = 0.2250 ft = 2.70 in. With ATBAT.UNDERCUT_FROM_JUDGE at 0.45, a vertical read error beyond 6.00 in puts the barrel past the ball. Nothing here is a fit; it is the intersection condition for a sphere and a cylinder.
contactGeometry.whyAHIGHConfidenceAtN1: A rulebook is not a sample and neither is a geometric identity -- the sim category's own exemption, which this record is entitled to only because it names its source (the circle-intersection condition) rather than asserting the number.
contactGeometry.whatItCost: A kid with contact 1 saturates beyond 0.74 sigma of his own vertical read, so 46% of his swings were arriving as vertical pop-ups instead of whiffs. Across the roster it was 30% of all fair balls.
contactGeometry.whatItMoved: Measured over 2,021 plate appearances on identical seeds, before and after: strikeout rate 20.6% -> 43.5%, whiff rate 9.3% -> 24.0%, BABIP 0.607 -> 0.709, and the batted-ball split from 48.7/10.9/11.4/29.0 (ground/line/fly/popup) to 58.7/15.5/14.8/11.0. ★ THE FIX TRADED A WRONG SHAPE FOR A WRONG RATE, DELIBERATELY: a 43% strikeout rate is one number a retune moves, whereas a spike at a boundary is a discontinuity no tuning constant can reach. And the old 20.6% was never right either -- it was arithmetic over a defect, since 30% of the balls it counted in play were swings that had missed.
contactGeometry.theOneCaseTheCLAMPSURVIVES: never_strikes_out. The ability already floors TIMING quality; a bat that misses on the VERTICAL axis would strike her out through the other door and make the ability a half-promise. She is pulled back to the edge of the barrel -- a real graze, and the worst contact the geometry allows -- rather than exempted from geometry. A test asserts she is alone in it.

ours.constant: src/v2/sim/contact.ts resolveSwing (the offset branch); src/v2/sim/params.ts BAT.BARREL_RADIUS_FT, ATBAT.UNDERCUT_FROM_JUDGE

contactGeometry.whatWouldClose: It is closed. The gate is contact.test.ts § 'a bat that misses the ball misses the ball', which sweeps undercuts past the barrel over the whole roster and requires max(|launchAngle|) < 90, plus harness.test.ts's boundary-pile-up check at the aggregate level.

battedBallSplit.what: How v2's batted balls divide into grounders, liners, flies and pop-ups, and the shape of the exit-velocity and launch-angle distributions behind that.
battedBallSplit.why: The roadmap asks the harness to assert the launch-angle split and exit-velocity shape 'against real baseball bands'. It measures them. It does not assert them, because the bands do not exist for this population -- see the partialReading.

partialReading.source: Broadcast/Statcast conventions for adult professional baseball.
partialReading.why: ★ QUARANTINED, AND THE QUARANTINE IS THE POINT. This is adults facing 90mph with a 32oz bat; ours are four-to-eight-year-olds facing 25.6mph. The two numbers are not comparable and the MLB column is here ONLY so a reader can see that ours is ground-heavier, which is what a child swinging under a pitch with a bat too heavy for them should produce. Conforming to it would be exactly the mistake sim.note names.
partialReading.andTheBINEDGESAREBORROWEDTOO: LAUNCH_CUTS (10 / 25 / 50 degrees) are the boundaries broadcast baseball reports itself with. Nothing about them is physics -- a ball at 9.9 degrees and one at 10.1 do the same thing -- and changing them changes the split without changing the sim. They are named here so that can never be mistaken for a measurement.

ours.over: 878 games / 50,004 plate appearances / 254,128 pitches, 8 seeds x 3 venues, all 30 kids

battedBallSplit.thereIsNoHardHitRate: Broadcast baseball calls a ball hard-hit at 95mph. The roster tops out near 61. The statistic would read zero for every kid forever, which is not a measurement -- and it is the MLB-contamination sim.note warns about wearing a number instead of a rate. The harness reports the distribution instead, and harness.ts says so in place of the field.
battedBallSplit.theFOULTOFAIRRATIOISAFINDING: 76,680 fouls against 23,076 fair balls -- 3.3 to 1, where real baseball is nearer 1 to 1. ATBAT.TWO_STRIKE_PROTECT_FT's own note predicted the mechanism from the other direction ('what balances strikeouts against fouls'), and it is currently balancing them toward both at once. ★ PR 9 DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX IT: the sweep showed the foul dial cannot be set without setting the strikeout rate, and the strikeout rate cannot be set without the defence -- see sim.retuneTargets.whyTheStrikeoutRateDidNotMoveHere. PR 10.
battedBallSplit.whatWouldClose: Batted-ball tracking from actual four-to-eight-year-old games -- the same afternoon with a sensor that would close sim.batSpeed would go most of the way, since a launch monitor reports angle and exit velocity together. Failing that, a published youth-baseball batted-ball profile at 8U or below; nothing found so far starts below 9U.
battedBallSplit.theSPLITISNOWSHAPEDBYAMECHANISM: ★ PR 8 MEASURED 60.2% GROUNDERS AND PR 9 FOUND OUT WHY: there was no swing plane, so the launch-angle distribution was symmetric about zero and the `ground` class -- everything below 10 degrees -- collected the whole negative half. 60% was arithmetic, not taste. With BAT.ATTACK_ANGLE_DEG at 8 the split is 49.8/16.0/18.2/16.0 and the launch MEAN is 8.0 rather than 0.0. sim.swingPlane has the derivation; the pop-up share is the one number that got worse and it is attributed there.

harnessMethod.what: How the statistical harness runs, what it costs, and -- the part worth reading -- what it cannot see.
harnessMethod.why: ★ A HARNESS THAT ONLY PINS IS A RATCHET, NOT A GATE. If every rate lands `awaiting-measurement` with ours pinned, the suite will happily enforce today's wrong BABIP forever. This record exists so that risk is written down next to the numbers rather than discovered later, and so the assertions that ARE falsifiable can be told apart from the ones that merely record.
harnessMethod.theSLICEAGREESWITHTHERUN: The CI slice and the full run share one aggregator, the way layout.browser.js is shared between the dev overlay and layout-audit.mjs -- a slice measuring something subtly different would be worse than no slice. Measured agreement over 2,021 PA against 50,045: strikeout rate 43.5 vs 43.0, BABIP 0.709 vs 0.713, ground-ball share 58.7 vs 60.2, exit-velocity mean 50.2 vs 50.2. The pinned bands in harness.test.ts are +-6pp, which is roughly twice the widest of those gaps.
harnessMethod.everyGameGetsItsOwnROOT: The per-plate-appearance fork key is `${inning}${half}${lineupIdx}`, which is NOT unique across games. Two simulateGame calls sharing a root produce byte-identical games, so a harness that forked one root per RUN would measure a single game 874 times and report it as a sample of 50,045. Both entry points seed per game.
harnessMethod.theROSTERROTATES: sim:game plays kids 0-8 against 9-17, so twelve of the thirty never bat -- and every rate here is a roster average over a stat span of 1-10. The window slides by 7 kids a game (coprime with 30, so it cycles fully) and the run is still deterministic.
whatItCannotSee: A HOME RUN AND AN INSIDE-THE-PARKER are one thing. tally.homeRuns has always meant 'the batter scored on his own ball', and splitting them needs play.ts's {t:'homeRun'} event, which runPlay does not harvest.

ANY HUMAN INPUT. Both sides are CPU, so this measures the sim's own physics and policies -- not what a six-year-old holding the device produces. The difficulty ladder, the fielding assist and the swing cursor are all outside it.

ERRORS AS A SEPARATE OUTCOME. A ball a fielder drops and a ball he never reached both arrive as a hit; v1's playground scoring rule (reaching on contact is a hit, errors included) is inherited deliberately, and stats.ts owns it.
SPRAY. The event stream carries the launch spec, so spray IS available, but nothing aggregates it yet -- pull/oppo balance is unmeasured.
harnessMethod.theASSERTIONSWITHTEETH: Ordering, not levels: a bad-contact lineup must strike out more and chase more than a good-contact one, and a high-power lineup must hit the ball harder and score more. Those are true of baseball and of any model worth shipping, and they need no band. Everything else in harness.test.ts is either internal consistency (the split sums to one; BABIP is hits over balls in play) or a pin.
harnessMethod.costDiscipline: #45's rule applies and was followed: remove the waste, then state a budget. PR 7's two fixes (the release solve memoised to a cache hit; the defence re-READING the ball without re-TRACING it) took a game from 1.7s to 0.14s, and the roster rotation plus warm memo now put it at 84ms. rng.ts promised 50k PA when it chose sfc32 over mulberry32; the run costs 73.5s, inside that. The full run carries RUN_BUDGET_MS (420s) as a hard ceiling -- a per-game timeout would miss a change that made every game four times slower.
harnessMethod.whatWouldClose: It does not close -- it is a `note` describing an instrument, the way instrument.* records describe the video one. It changes when the harness does.

retuneTargets.what: What the retune is aiming AT, written down before anything was swept.
retuneTargets.why: ★ THESE ARE DESIGN TARGETS FOR A GAME FOR FOUR-TO-EIGHT-YEAR-OLDS, NOT CONFORMANCE TO A MEASUREMENT NOBODY TOOK. That distinction is the entire reason this record exists and is a `note` rather than a band. There is no published plate-discipline or batted-ball data below 9U (sim.plateDiscipline, sim.battedBallSplit, sim.batSpeed all say so from their own directions), and sim.note's warning is explicit: conforming a game for this age group to MLB's strikeout rate is THE failure the `reference` field exists to prevent. So the alternative to a borrowed band is not a better band -- it is an honest design choice, argued and signed.
retuneTargets.whyWrittenFIRST: ★ A TARGET FITTED AFTER THE SWEEP IS NOT A TARGET, IT IS A DESCRIPTION. Four coupled constants are being moved (ATTACK_ANGLE_DEG, UNDERCUT_FROM_JUDGE, PULL_DEG_PER_FT, TWO_STRIKE_PROTECT_FT) and any of them can be walked toward almost any pair of numbers. Committing the targets before running the sweep is what makes the sweep a search rather than a rationalisation -- the same discipline pace.pitchCorridor applies when it refuses to promote an n=1 reading, and the same one that made PR 8 pin a BABIP of .713 it did not like.

after_pr9.over: 878 games / 50,004 plate appearances / 254,128 pitches, 8 seeds x 3 venues, all 30 kids

theArgumentForEACHONE.strikeouts: 15-20% against a measured 43.0%. The product is a voting machine for 30 characters and its design pillars are 'minimal reading, short games, be genuinely fun' -- a six-year-old who makes an out without swinging half the time is not voting, they are watching. 15-20% is BELOW real baseball's ~22% on purpose: the fun of this game is contact.
theArgumentForEACHONE.walks: Left roughly where it is. A walk is already the least interesting outcome available and nothing in the measurement suggests it is wrong.
theArgumentForEACHONE.fouls: 3.43 fouls per fair ball means the median plate appearance spends most of its pitches going nowhere, which is what pushes pitches/PA to 5.12. Real baseball runs nearer 1:1. Targeting 1-2 keeps the foul as a real event -- ATBAT.TWO_STRIKE_PROTECT_FT exists precisely so a poor-contact kid becomes a foul-ball machine rather than a strikeout machine -- without it being the modal outcome.
theArgumentForEACHONE.groundShare: 40-50% against 60.2%. This one is NOT primarily a taste judgement: 60% is what a zero-mean launch-angle distribution produces mechanically, because the `ground` class is everything below 10 degrees and therefore the entire negative half. See sim.swingPlane. The target is what a swing with a real attack angle gives, and the range is wide because the exact figure is a consequence rather than a dial.
theArgumentForEACHONE.launchMedian: 7-14 degrees against 2.5. Same mechanism, stated in the units the defect actually lives in.

retuneTargets.whatIsNOTATARGETHERE: BABIP. It is .713 and it is wrong, but it belongs to the DEFENCE and the defence is the next PR. Moving the batted-ball mix will move it as a side effect -- fewer grounders is fewer of the class that goes for hits 81.4% of the time -- and this record must report by how much WITHOUT claiming credit for a fix it did not make. Tuning a plate constant until BABIP looks right would be fixing a defence symptom through the batter, which is the same category of error as fixing the strikeout rate by clamping a bat that had missed.
retuneTargets.theGATEISORDERING: ★ AND IT IS NOT ANY OF THE NUMBERS ABOVE. A retune that hits all six targets and makes a good-contact kid strike out MORE than a bad-contact one has broken the model, and only harness.test.ts's ordering assertions would say so. Those must survive the retune untouched; if one has to move, the retune is wrong and not the assertion.
retuneTargets.whatWouldClose: It does not close -- it is a `note` recording a design decision and the state it was taken from. PR 10 answers the three targets PR 9 left: strikeouts, fouls and pitches per plate appearance, together with the defence, because the sweep proved they cannot be answered apart from it. The record is superseded outright when someone measures real four-to-eight-year-old baseball.
retuneTargets.whyTheStrikeoutRateDidNotMoveHere: ★ THE SWEEP FOUND THAT 43% STRIKEOUTS IS LOAD-BEARING, and that is the most important thing this record now carries. The four constants WERE swept together as planned (scripts/v2/plate-sweep.mjs, 300 combinations), and several combinations hit all six targets at once -- attack 9 / undercut 0.22 / pull 16 / protect 0.55 gives K 15.4%, foul:fair 1.81, ground 50.5%. Measured at n=40 against the same seeds, that combination also takes RUNS PER GAME FROM 4.90 TO 15.35. The strikeout rate is currently doing the work the defence cannot: three times as many balls in play against a defence that converts under a third of them is a 15-run game. So the plate targets ALONE are under-determined -- they admit solutions that wreck the product -- and the strikeout and foul targets moved to PR 10, where they can be balanced against out conversion. That is the only place the balance can honestly be struck; striking it here would have meant PR 10 tuning a defence against a plate that was itself tuned blind to outs.
retuneTargets.whatPR9SHIPPED: The swing plane alone (sim.swingPlane) -- a MISSING MECHANIC rather than a dial. It hits the two batted-ball targets, and BABIP and runs per game both improve as a side effect. Nothing regressed except the pop-up share, which is measured against the dial that fixes it. A retune that improves every measured axis but one, and can say which pending change owns that one, is a different kind of change from a retune that hits its targets by moving four constants at once.

swingPlane.what: The upward tilt of the bat's path through the zone -- the attack angle -- and the fact that until PR 9 there wasn't one.
swingPlane.why: ★ THE AVERAGE BATTED BALL LEFT AT EXACTLY 0 DEGREES, FOR FOUR PRs. atbat.ts computes the undercut as `(crossing.y - judged.y) * UNDERCUT_FROM_JUDGE`, and `judged.y` is `crossing.y + bell() * judgeFt` -- so the undercut is `-bell() * judgeFt * k`, which is EXACTLY zero-mean. contact.ts takes asin of it, so the launch-angle distribution was symmetric about zero BY CONSTRUCTION. Every kid in the game swung dead level. This is the same class of defect as isFair having no caller and Rng.bell's bounded support hiding the whiff rate: a mechanic that was never built, presenting as a number that merely looks wrong.
swingPlane.howItHid: ★ NO TOTAL COULD SEE IT AND NEITHER COULD THE MEDIAN. The ground-ball class is everything below 10 degrees, which includes the entire negative half of a symmetric distribution, so a 60.2% ground share was not a mistuning -- it was arithmetic. The launch MEDIAN read 2.5 degrees, which looks merely low rather than structurally impossible. PR 8 measured and pinned both without either being recognised as a missing mechanic; it took asking why the median was where it was. `harness.ts` now reports a MEAN, which is the one statistic that reads 0 when there is no swing plane, and harness.test.ts asserts it is positive.

partialReading.source: Bat-sensor aggregates and coaching benchmarks for adult and amateur hitters (Blast Motion, Rapsodo-class swing tracking).
partialReading.why: ★ QUARANTINED ON THE sim.batSpeed PRECEDENT, and for the identical reason. Attack angle is a real, routinely-measured property of a swing -- but every source measures adults or high-school-and-up amateurs. NOBODY HAS PUT A BAT SENSOR ON A FOUR-YEAR-OLD. Our 8 degrees is the bottom of the adult band, chosen because a child swinging a bat that is heavy for them has less ability to hold an upward plane, and that reasoning is an argument rather than a measurement.

swingPlane.itIsNOTThePitchDescentAngle: ★ THE TEMPTING DERIVATION, AND IT IS WRONG. Measured off our own releasePitch/flyToPlate: our pitches arrive at the plate descending 22.2-39.9 degrees (mean 28.1), because a 25.6mph lob over 46ft falls a long way. A swing matched to the pitch plane -- the textbook 'swing along the plane of the pitch' -- would give an attack angle near 28 and put essentially everything in the air. A real attack angle is a property of the SWING, measured independently of what is being swung at, which is why this record answers to reference: 'baseball' and not to our own sim.pitchCorridorV2.
swingPlane.theFRAMEARGUMENT: The undercut is a displacement measured PERPENDICULAR TO THE BAT'S PATH -- it is where the barrel's centre passed relative to the ball's centre. So `asin(undercut / centreSep)` is an angle in the BAT's frame, and the swing plane's own tilt adds to it to reach the world frame. That is a statement about which coordinate system the geometry was already in, not a fudge term bolted on to move a number.

whatItMoved.over: 878 games / 50,004 plate appearances / 254,128 pitches, 8 seeds x 3 venues, all 30 kids
whatItMoved.note: BABIP and runs both IMPROVED as a side effect -- fewer grounders is fewer of the class that goes for hits 81.4% of the time -- and this record claims no credit for a defence fix it did not make. The strikeout rate barely moved, correctly: a swing plane changes where a struck ball goes, not whether it is struck.

swingPlane.theONENUMBERTHATGOTWORSE: Pop-ups, 10.0% -> 16.0%. Centring a distribution whose SPREAD is still too wide pushes its upper tail past 50 degrees. The spread is ATBAT.UNDERCUT_FROM_JUDGE (0.45, untouched here), and it is measured rather than hoped: at attack 8, narrowing the undercut 0.45 -> 0.30 -> 0.22 takes pop-ups 15.9% -> 9.5% -> 3.7%. PR 10 owns that dial, so the cost is attributable to a specific pending change rather than left as a regression nobody can explain.
swingPlane.whatWouldClose: A bat sensor on three or more actual four-to-eight-year-olds -- the SAME afternoon at a tee-ball practice that would close sim.batSpeed, since a Blast Motion or Diamond Kinetics knob sensor reports attack angle and bat speed from one swing. Two records close together or neither does.

defense.note: Constants governing the CPU defense. SCALED 1.987x with RUNNER_SPEED in the 2026-07-24 retune but STILL NOT MEASURED -- they are the values most likely to need feel iteration, because halving runner speed doubles the time the defense has and the scaling assumes BB's defense is slow in the same proportion its runners are. If the retune plays wrong, start here. As of 2026-07-28 the first of them HAS been retuned: see fielderSpeed, which was the one constant in this block that had no record at all.

fielderSpeed.what: How fast a fielder runs, expressed against the pace anchor: fielders and baserunners are THE SAME KIDS, so the honest ratio is 1.0. A kid does not get faster by putting a glove on.
fielderSpeed.comparisonForm: fielder speed / runner speed -- both px/s in the same space, so the ratio is dimensionless and survives BB being 640x480 while we are 960x640. Reads as plain English: 'a fielder runs N times as fast as a baserunner.' Sanity band: 0.9x-1.4x. Outside that, one of the two is wrong -- and it sat at 2.48x through every retune of the constant it is measured against.
fielderSpeed.whatWouldWork: THIS ONE IS ACTUALLY MEASURABLE, unlike its neighbours in this block. defense.throwSpeed and defense.cpuThrowDelay are blocked on tracking a ~5px ball; a RUNNING FIELDER is a big sprite crossing open grass, the same target class as the runner in pace.homeToFirst (which reached n=3). Method: pick a fielder breaking for a ball on a capture that passes video.js clockFidelity, read first-motion and arrival frames magnified >=2x (flags=neighbor -- at 1x a pose change reads as motion, the exact trap that produced the withdrawn 270ms pitch corridor), convert px/s against the same basepath scale pace.homeToFirst used, and divide by 48.17px/s. n>=3 before promoting: the repo's own n<3 rule exists because overclaiming is how the 270 happened.
fielderSpeed.invariant: cpuFielderSpeedMult MUST equal playerRunSpeedMult in every mode. That is what holds the ratio on the side the human BATS, and its absence is what let kid mode drift to its own separate value (0.62) that happened to compensate for a base that was 2.48x too high.
fielderSpeed.retuneNote: FIELDER_SPEED 106 -> 42.8 px/s (ratio 2.48x -> 1.0x) and MODES.kid.live.cpuFielderSpeedMult 0.62 -> 1.3. Kid mode's ABSOLUTE CPU fielder speed barely moved (65.7 -> 55.6): it was the one branch already near 1.0x, because the 0.62 was silently cancelling most of the bad base. DERIVED, not measured -- this record claims nothing about BB.
fielderSpeed.history: The most useful thing in this record. FIELDER_SPEED sat at 210 px/s through FIVE consecutive runner slowdowns -- 280fe50 175 (1.20x), 67b9d87 150 (1.40x), 164cd55 117 (1.79x), 96f320e 106 (1.98x), 7a859ca 85 (2.47x) -- and the 2026-07-24 retune (4b93867) then scaled BOTH by 1/1.987, faithfully preserving 2.48x. Every time the defense could not get outs the fix was 'slow the runners', never 'check the fielder'. Two commit titles say it outright: 'Rebalance the fielding race: throwing runners out is finally possible' and 'Backyard-pace the fielding race: slower runners and ball, snappier throws'. Nothing caught it because this was the ONLY pace constant with no record here and no pin in conformance.test.js -- every neighbour had both. The lesson is not 'someone typed a wrong number'; it is that an ungoverned constant absorbs the error of every governed one around it.
fielderSpeed.symptom: An outfielder could charge into the infield, field the ball, and still beat the batter to first -- carry speed equals chase speed with no penalty (liveplay.ts moveFielders), so running the ball in was a viable defensive play. At 106px/s a center fielder carried it to the plate (268px) in 2.5s against a 4.2s basepath leg. The slowest possible fielder (84.8px/s) outran the fastest possible baserunner (55.6px/s) by 1.5x.
fielderSpeed.exposed: Slower fielders surfaced TWO latent bugs that faster ones had been hiding. (1) Doubling a runner off a caught fly ONLY ever worked via the carrier footracing them for a tag -- the CPU's throw path was gated behind cpuThrowDelayMs + CATCH_GATHER_MS (1192 + 1100 = 2292ms), which no throw-behind can beat. Fixed in liveplay.ts catchGatherFor: the gather beat is about runners ADVANCING (it is what makes a sac fly a real race) and does not apply to a throw behind a runner scrambling back. (2) The maxPlayMs straggler settle read `r.from`, but reverseLeg SWAPS from/to -- so a runner turned back from the plate carries from === 4 while running toward third, having never touched home. They settled standing ON home with no run scored, and finishLivePlay writes bases[3] on a 3-element tuple, so the runner silently vanished from the inning. Fixed to settle on min(from, to), clamped 1-3. Longer plays (slower fielders reach maxPlayMs far more often) are what made a latent edge case reachable; the random send/hold property test caught it only stochastically, so it is now pinned deterministically at the seam.
fielderSpeed.notSufficient: THIS DOES NOT MAKE BASE HITS POSSIBLE, and saying so here is the point of the record. Measured against the real sim after the change (CLASSIC, human batting, CPU fielding, stat-5 batter, 4197ms leg): routine grounder to SS out by 1397ms, slow roller to 3B out by 347ms, ball through the 5-6 hole out by 1047ms, TRUE LF-CF gap out by 897ms, TRUE CF-RF gap out by 1097ms, down the RF line out by 2047ms. Every ball a fielder reaches is still a putout at first. What the ratio fix DID close is the specific pathology it was aimed at: the carry. A center fielder ran the ball to the plate in 2.53s and to first in 1.94s, against a 4.2s leg; those are now 6.26s and 4.81s, so running it in is dead, and at 42.8px/s a fielder can no longer outrun a grounder (GROUNDER_SPEED 81-121px/s) and must intercept instead.
fielderSpeed.nextLever: defense.throwSpeed, NOT this record. The binding term on a batter-to-first race is the fixed overhead plus the throw, not the chase: cpuReactionMs 835 + cpuThrowDelayMs 1192 = 2027ms of standing still (48% of the whole leg), then a ~480ms throw. The dimensionless tell is in defense.throwSpeed.comparisonForm: CLASSIC throws at 9.65x runner speed where KID -- the mode that actually produces base hits -- throws at 4.60x (413 x 0.62 = 256 vs its 55.64px/s runner). Two modes sitting at 9.65x and 4.60x inside a 3x-20x sanity band is exactly the kind of internal inconsistency that band exists to surface.
fielderSpeed.structuralNote: A deeper reason no single speed constant separates hits from outs: our outfield is too shallow relative to the diamond. CF sits 268px from home against a 179.6px basepath -- a 1.5x ratio, where real baseball is ~3.3x. So an outfielder's throw is barely longer than an infielder's (SS->1B 229px vs CF->1B 206px -- the OUTFIELDER's is SHORTER), and throw distance cannot discriminate. Down the RF line is out by 2047ms, FASTER than the routine grounder to short, because 1B is standing right there. Any real fix to offense has to touch geometry.FIELD_POSITIONS or the throw ratio, not the chase.

cpuReaction.what: Delay between contact and the fielding team actually breaking for the ball.

partialReading.method: Background-subtracted fielder tracks (kids are ~20x35 native, so the size filter that cannot isolate a 5px ball works cleanly on them), decimated to distinct frames, linked with lib.js linkTracks. Reaction = first frame the biggest-moving infielder has left its start by >6px and stays gone. Grounders specifically: on a FLY the chaser often does not move at all, because BB paints the landing disc where the ball will go and the nearest fielder is frequently already standing on it -- fly plays gave 817-3283ms of noise for exactly that reason.
partialReading.why: NOT promoted, for two reasons that are about the measurement rather than the spread. (1) DEFINITIONAL: a displacement threshold cannot separate a DECISION DELAY from an ACCELERATION RAMP. Our cpuReactionMs is a deliberate AI pause; if BB's fielders instead start immediately and accelerate slowly, the same 1050ms would be measuring something we do not model, and scaling our constant to it would be wrong. An eye read of play-15 shows a fielder genuinely STATIC for ~0.67s and then breaking, which favours a real delay -- but that is n=1 and not enough to settle it. (2) IDENTIFICATION: without ball tracking the PRIMARY fielder cannot be picked out reliably, and 'biggest mover' also selects kids who are backing up or covering a base, which is different behaviour with its own timing.
partialReading.whatWouldResolveIt: Per-play eye reads on grounders: watch the fielder who actually gathers the ball, and check whether he holds a standing pose for a beat (decision delay) or shifts into a run pose immediately and covers ground slowly (acceleration ramp). BB's pose set makes that visible -- it is the same read that settled the fly hang. Roughly one sheet per play across the five grounders.

cpuReaction.ifItHolds: Taken at face value the partial reading is ~2.5x our 420ms, which is the same direction and rough size as every other measured pace drift (run 0.50x, between-pitch 0.49x). That consistency is suggestive, and it is NOT evidence -- three separate clean-looking numbers were wrong this session before being looked at.

poseEvidence.finding: play-15, 33ms sheet from the cut: the fielding kid holds a STANDING pose for ~0.67s and only then shifts to a run pose and covers ground.
poseEvidence.implication: That favours a real DECISION DELAY -- something comparable to our cpuReactionMs -- rather than a pure acceleration ramp, which is the confound that keeps this record from being promoted.
poseEvidence.why: n=1 is not enough to promote. One fielder on one play could be hesitating for a reason specific to that play (the ball was hit elsewhere, he is not the primary). The read is cheap and repeatable though: the same 33ms sheet on plays 03/04/12/17 would settle it, and the partialReading's five samples are already waiting for that verdict.

cpuThrowDelay.what: How long a CPU fielder holds the ball before releasing a throw.

blocked.finding: Needs the BALL: the beat is 'fielder gathers it' -> 'ball separates and accelerates away'. Ball tracking in the wide view is the open problem recorded in instrument.background-subtraction and pace.flyHang -- the fly hang was measured off the landing DISC precisely because the ball itself is not reliably trackable there.
blocked.whatWouldWork: The gather and release are both visible as POSE changes on a large sprite (glove-down, then throw). Reading those by eye sidesteps ball tracking entirely, and is the same technique that would settle defense.cpuReaction. Not reached.

blocked.finding: THE CLEANEST TARGET DOES NOT EXIST IN THIS CAPTURE. The plan was catcher->2B on a steal, where both endpoints are measured bases (220.4px, zero geometry inference). chaserElection.what: WHICH fielder chases a loose ball is now a decision with its own constants, not a fixed consequence of geometry. Recorded because the two obvious metrics both fail, and both failures are cheap to rediscover and expensive to diagnose.
chaserElection.finding: Ranking candidates by 'who can reach the ball soonest' hands essentially every grounder to the PITCHER. A grounder starts at HOME and rolls outward, so P -- 112px from the plate -- is nearest its early path at every spray angle, and wins the race to cut it off before anyone else is close. Adding a distance-to-settle penalty term does not separate them (swept lambda 0..8 ms/px, no crossover). Gating candidacy on the SETTLE point instead does: the pitcher is simply not a candidate for a ball that comes to rest 122px+ from the mound, which is what a real defense does. But that alone is still not enough -- a third baseman can genuinely reach a ball rolling AT the shortstop 125-257ms sooner by charging across in front of him. True on the clock, wrong on a ball field. So the ball belongs to whoever's zone it settles in, and a challenger must beat that fielder by CUT_AHEAD_MS.

measuredWindow.how: Cut-off times computed against the real predictLoosePath and the real fielder speeds for four reference launches (grounder settling at the shortstop's feet at two roll speeds, the shallow-right grounder that motivated the work, and a comebacker). Below 257 the third-baseman-poaches-shortstop case returns; above 523 the second baseman stops cutting off the shallow-right grounder and it dribbles through to the outfielder.
measuredWindow.stabilityClaimCorrected: 2026-07-28. This block used to end 'Stable across both kid and main fielder speeds.' That held over the range it was tested at -- kid 65.7px/s vs main 106px/s, a 1.6x spread -- and is NOT a general claim. CUT_AHEAD_MS is a fixed ms gate compared (fielding.ts electChaser: `c.ms + CUT_AHEAD_MS >= ownerMs`) against BALL-PATH times returned by cutOff(). Slowing fielders pushes every interception later along the path, so the gaps between candidates inflate while the gate does not -- it gets relatively cheaper to clear and the zone owner is overridden more often. It cannot be speed-neutral by construction.
measuredWindow.measuredDrift: Swept a 20px grid of grounder settle points x 4 roll speeds (n=1372), counting how often electChaser returns someone other than the fielder whose POST is nearest the settle point: at 106px/s + 400ms the owner is overridden 27.7% of the time; at 42.8px/s + 400ms, 32.4%. A 4.7-point drift -- real, and far smaller than a first-principles estimate suggests, which is why it was measured rather than assumed.
measuredWindow.whyNotRetunedAt42_8: Restoring 27.7% needs CUT_AHEAD_MS ~600 (measured: 600 -> 26.5%), which is ABOVE this record's own upperBound of 523 -- past which the second baseman stops cutting off the shallow-right grounder. But that bound was itself derived at 106px/s and moves with the speed too, so 600 is not knowably safe, only knowably outside a stale window. BOTH bounds must be re-derived at 42.8px/s against the same four reference launches before this constant moves. Left at 400 deliberately: a measured 4.7-point drift is not worth trading for an unmeasured bound violation.

chaserElection.why: BB2001 was NOT measured for this. The election is tuned against baseball sense and our own geometry, not against a capture -- the same standing caveat as the rest of the defense block. It also makes the CPU defense meaningfully better on grounders (it cuts balls off instead of trailing them), so it is a live candidate for the first feel-tuning pass. Lower CUTOFF_GRACE_MS first (fewer cut-offs), then the corner/middle leashes -- not cpuFielderSpeedMult, which is on the scaled pace path and would desynchronise it.

fieldingAssist.what: How much CLASSIC's magnet assist steers the player's fielder toward the ball, now scaled per difficulty tier rather than one flat constant.
fieldingAssist.why: Recorded because the flat 0.5 blend was not a mild helper -- it was the whole play. Measured against the real sim: steering PERPENDICULAR to a fly for its entire hang time still left the fielder 5.3px from the landing spot, well inside the 39px catch reach. The game caught the ball for you no matter where you pointed, so defense had no skill in it. At the tiered blends the same deliberate mis-steer ends 102px off on MEDIUM and 189px off on HARD -- both clean misses.
invariants: The magnet lerps between two candidate points each within one movement step, so it can only REDIRECT, never add speed. A liveplay test pins the per-tick cap at every tier.

assistIdleSpeedMult must stay < 1 at every tier. The idle amble is only fair while it is worse than steering, and that is a RELATIVE claim -- weakening the magnet without also slowing the amble would have made doing nothing the optimal defense on HARD. That is why the hard tier scales its idle knobs alongside its magnet.
fieldingAssist.whatWouldWork: BB2001's assist strength has no on-screen representation -- nothing renders it, so no frame can be read for it, exactly like the swing windows (see pace.swingWindows). It could only be inferred behaviourally: drive BB's fielder along a fixed WRONG heading through a fly's full hang time on a known field, and measure how far the sprite drifts from its own steering line toward the landing spot. That needs frame-accurate input injection into the emulator, which this instrument does not have. Until then these are feel dials, tuned by playing -- not conformance targets.
